analysis.title: American Electric Power (AEP): First Take: 3Q26 EPS beat; $100 bn capital plan and 10%+ EPS CAGR through 2031 announced
key_insights: AEP reported 3Q26 ongoing EPS of $2.23, versus GSe and FactSet consensus of $2.06, a $0.18 variance to GS's estimate.
AEP now expects 2026 EPS at or above the high end of its $6.25-$6.55 guidance range. GS forecasts $6.42.
AEP introduced a $100 bn 2027-2031 capital plan, up from the prior $78 bn 2026-2030 plan.
AEP raised its growth outlook to 9%-11% annual EPS growth and a 10%+ CAGR through 2031, versus 9%+ through 2030 previously.
New 2027/2028 EPS guidance is $6.75-$7.05 and $7.40-$7.70, versus GS estimates of $7.05 and $7.73.
Contracted load rose to 84 GW through 2031 from 69 GW last quarter, driven by about 15 GW of new electric service agreements (ESAs).
Piketon is now included in the transmission capital plan. The roughly $4 bn Wyoming fuel-cell project is backed by a 20-year PPA with Google and targeted for in-service by year-end 2028.

The beat versus GS was driven by higher operating income, as stronger gross margin more than offset higher O&M, D&A and taxes other than income. Lower interest expense also helped, and taxes were broadly in line.
By segment, G&M drove most of the upside ($0.19 vs GS $0.05), with smaller beats from T&D and VIU. Transco was in line and Corporate & Other came in below GS's estimate.

GS expects the call to focus on the new five-year capital and financing plan, incremental capex and the 45 GW Batch Zero submission following the Texas data center audit, and regulatory updates on I&M's Indiana rate case and large load tariff proceedings.

GS key call questions: whether Texas data-center customers have resized or delayed projects since the state audit, how much of the 84 GW contracted load is in the $100 bn plan, and how PSO, SWEPCO and APCo generation procurements are progressing.
GS rates AEP Neutral with a 12-month SOTP-based price target of $146, about 12.0% upside from the $130.30 close on 27 Oct 2026.

market_movers.rationale: GS stays Neutral with a $146 SOTP-based target after the 3Q26 beat and the larger $100 bn capital plan. The target was last set at $146 on 15-Oct-26.

earnings_insights: 3Q26 ongoing EPS reported $2.23 versus GS estimate and FactSet consensus of $2.06 (reported 28 Oct 2026).
2026 EPS guidance: AEP now expects at or above the high end of its $6.25-$6.55 range. GS estimate is $6.42.
2027 EPS guidance introduced at $6.75-$7.05 versus GS estimate of $7.05. 2028 guidance is $7.40-$7.70 versus GS estimate of $7.73.
3Q26 ongoing net income $1,216 mn reported versus GS est $1,145 mn. Gross margin was $4,776 mn versus GS est $4,330 mn, and total revenues were $6,863 mn versus $6,166 mn.
3Q26 segment EPS reported versus GS est: VIU $1.32 vs $1.30, T&D $0.52 vs $0.48, G&M $0.19 vs $0.05, Transco $0.40 vs $0.41, Corp & Other ($0.20) vs ($0.18).
GS EPS estimates: $6.42 for 2026E, $7.05 for 2027E, $7.73 for 2028E, versus $5.94 in 2025. Next quarter, 4Q26E EPS is $1.39.
risk_factors: Financing needs for the larger capital plan.
Failure to close the ROE gap at the VIU utilities.
Adverse regulatory decisions in key jurisdictions such as Texas or Ohio on data center tariffs could hurt utility returns.
Upside risks: faster interconnection of contracted load, or larger realization of Bloom/Piketon and other incremental capex beyond what GS already embeds.
